customManagers.description: Treat the pnpm base image tag in Dockerfile as the `pnpm` npm dependency that `packageManager` in package.json pins. Sharing the dep name and datasource gives both one release-age clock and one branch (`renovate/pnpm-<major>.x`), so the tag moves in the same PR as `packageManager`. Grouping the docker datasource with the npm package (as `group:pnpm` does) is not enough: Renovate gets no release timestamp for ghcr.io tags, so the image never clears `minimumReleaseAge` and the group PR ships the npm bump alone while the tag waits in Pending Status Checks. The image is published a few minutes after the npm release, well within the release age. Renovate runs `matchStrings` over the whole file without the multiline flag, so the pattern ends in `\s` rather than `$`.

packageRules.description: The dockerfile manager still sees the pnpm base image as a docker dependency; leave that view switched off so it cannot open a second, unsynchronised PR for the same tag

Give the Dockerfile copy of `pnpm` the same settings as the shared preset’s rule for `packageManager`, which only matches the npm manager. A branch waits for dashboard approval if any of its updates does and is merged automatically only if all of them are, so without this the joint PR would wait for approval.
